name: thumbnail-taste
summary: Brand-neutral taste rules for video thumbnails and vertical covers, drawn from two 2026 thumbnail studies, YouTube's own testing docs, official safe-zone files and 18 observed gaming and tutorial thumbnails. One clear idea per thumbnail, the result shown in use, an outcome promised in a few words, and everything kept inside each platform's safe area. Colors, fonts, logo and art come from the project's brand kit in /thumbs/brand.json.

principles.title: One idea that reads at sidebar size
principles.rule: One subject and one promise. Check it at 168 px wide (and 130 px for grids). If you have to explain it, cut it.
principles.why: Large studies find winners and losers look alike on surface features, so the edge is a clear idea, not effects (measured). The weakest tutorials in the observed examples cram three messages into one frame and sit at 0.5x (observed).

principles.title: Four words is the target, six the ceiling
principles.rule: 0 to 4 words by default, up to 6 if it is one phrase. Never a sentence, never a list.
principles.why: Eden: 4 to 6 words had the largest lead for breakouts (30.6% vs 26.5%), 7+ words trailed (29.6% vs 31.1%). vidIQ: median 5 words among breakouts with text, and 52% used 0 to 3 (measured).

principles.title: Thumbnail adds, title explains
principles.rule: The title holds the search words (product, task, platform, version). The thumbnail holds the outcome or the hook. Do not repeat the title.
principles.why: Viewers read thumbnail and title together (ETRA 2018). Verbatim repeats are rare among breakouts (6.3%, measured). The leaked MrBeast guide treats both as one expectation.

principles.title: Show it in use, not the menu
principles.rule: Show the result happening: the finished thing, people using it, the moment itself. Not a settings screen or a logo on a backdrop. When the video is about doing something together or against each other, put two or more people in one frame and mark them apart: tags, name labels, outline colors, a 4 VS 1.
principles.why: The multiplayer outliers in the observed examples all do this: P1/P2 tags at 6.4x, tagged pets as players, a 4 VS 1 at 7.6M views (observed, one niche). 1of10: multiple faces beat a single face (measured, second hand).

principles.title: A face is optional, a clear subject is not
principles.rule: Use a real face only with a real reaction. Otherwise the product, a character or the finished result is the subject. No stock shocked faces.
principles.why: Faces barely separate winners: 84.2% vs 82.2%, inside noise (Eden); 1of10 finds it niche dependent; only 5% of breakouts use exaggerated expressions (vidIQ). The server tutorial winners at 20x+ in the observed examples use game art, not faces (observed, one niche).

principles.title: Tutorials promise an outcome, a time or a price
principles.rule: Name what the viewer gets: FREE, IN 5 MIN, YOUR OWN [THING], DONE. Not the process: INSTALLING, CONFIGURING, PART 1.
principles.why: FREE VALHEIM SERVER did 25.6x on a 1.1K sub channel, IN 5 MINUTES 6.5x, FULL SERVER BY AI 32.7x (observed, one niche). MrBeast guide: pick the most interesting version of the idea.

principles.title: Name the subject at a glance
principles.rule: A logo, the product, a recognizable character or a signature place tells the viewer what the video is about before they read a word. Your own wordmark is secondary and small.
principles.why: Nearly every tutorial outlier in the observed examples shows the logo of the thing it covers, large (observed, one niche). People search by subject, not by channel.

principles.title: Separate the subject, keep the palette small
principles.rule: The subject and the words stand clear of a calm ground, with one accent color from the brand kit. No field of YouTube red, white or black.
principles.why: Average brightness, contrast and saturation do not separate winners (Eden), but 89% of breakouts have a face or high contrast (vidIQ): separation matters, raw brightness does not. 1of10 suggests about 3 colors (vendor claim).

principles.title: Only promise what the video shows early
principles.rule: Every number, time, price and feature on the thumbnail must be true and visible in the first minute. Real names and counts on an info card.
principles.why: Test & Compare picks on watch time share, not CTR, so a bait variant loses the test. The MrBeast guide ties mismatch to lower retention.

principles.title: Test three ideas, not three tints
principles.rule: The three Test & Compare variants differ in concept (subject, promise, proof), not font or color.
principles.why: Similar variants end as Performed same or run long (YouTube). One gaming channel moved CTR 4.2% to 7.8% with a full concept change (single vendor case, unverified).

principles.title: One recognizable series frame
principles.rule: Keep one look for a series (frame, type, accent, logo placement) and change the subject per video.
principles.why: One channel's two server guides share a framed card and run 23x and 27x its median (observed).

principles.title: One arrow, only if it explains
principles.rule: An arrow links two things (before to after, cause to effect). Never decoration, never two.
principles.why: Drawn graphics sit just above noise (41.8% vs 38.1%, Eden). The observed guides that use an arrow use one, to show cause and effect.

principles.title: Keep words out of UI and crop zones
principles.rule: Words and faces inside the platform safe rect, clear of the duration badge, grid crops, view counts and X's domain label.
principles.why: Official safe zone files from Google, TikTok and Meta, Buffer on the Instagram grid, TechCrunch on X link cards.

principles.title: A vertical cover is a poster, not a frame
principles.rule: Center on x 50, keep words between about 22% and 65% of the height. Design for the grid and shelf, then check the first frame against playback UI.
principles.why: Shorts thumbnails show on the homepage and channel tab, not in the Shorts feed, and cannot be A/B tested (PPC Land). Grids crop to 3:4 or square and add view counts.

rubric.question: At 168 px wide, can a stranger say what this video gives them within 3 seconds?
Does it show the result in use (the finished thing, people doing it) instead of a menu, a settings screen or a lone logo?
Do the words name an outcome, time, price or stakes in 6 words or fewer, without repeating the title?
Will the first minute of the video confirm every claim on it?
Is the subject recognizable at a glance from a logo, product, character or place?
Does the subject stand clear of a calm ground with one accent color, and no red, white or black field?
Are all words and faces inside the safe rect and clear of hard zones for this platform?
Is this variant a different idea from the other two in the test?

notes: Design at 1920x1080, upload 1280x720 or larger. Judge at 168 px wide (sidebar) and about 120 px (mobile).
The duration badge covers the bottom right at every size; at sidebar size it is about a fifth of the width.
Test & Compare: up to 3 variants, desktop Studio, winner by watch time share. Not available for Shorts.
Title and thumbnail are read together: the title keeps the search words, the thumbnail the hook.

zones.label: Duration badge (approx, sized for the 168 px sidebar)
Watch later and queue icons on hover

notes: The cover is seen in grids and shelves (cropped, with view counts). Playback UI only covers the first frame, so those zones are soft.
Shorts custom thumbnails show on the homepage and channel Shorts tab, not in the Shorts feed. No A/B testing for Shorts.
Safe rect x 192 to 888, y 420 to 1248 clears Shorts, TikTok and Reels playback UI and a centered square grid crop. Center everything on x 50.
TikTok's action rail (x 780 to 960 from y 840) clips the lower right of the safe rect: keep that corner free of words.
Judge at 130 px wide (profile grid). The TikTok grid crop (square vs 3:4) is disputed; the safe rect assumes the stricter square.

notes: The feed shows the full 4:5. Buffer says the grid previews posts at 4:5; 3:4 tiles would trim about 34 px per side (uncertain).
Some accounts still see the square grid: keep words inside the center 1080x1080.
Reddit shows 4:5 images whole in most feeds (observed): the same layout works there.

zones.label: Carousel or Reel icon in the grid (approx)

notes: A square post shows whole in the feed. Judge at 130 px wide (profile grid).
Instagram's grid tiles are 3:4, so a square image can lose up to 135 px on each side there (derived from the tile ratio, unverified). The safe rect keeps words inside x 150 to 930.
Native 16:9 images show whole in the X timeline (observed). Judge at 350 px wide.
Shared as a link card, X crops toward 1.91:1 and puts a small domain label bottom left, with no headline since Oct 2023.
Reddit link thumbnails are tiny: post the image natively (16:9 or 4:5) instead.

zones.label: ALT badge when alt text is set (approx)

do: Name the outcome: FREE, IN 5 MIN, DONE, YOUR OWN [THING].
Use true numbers: counts, minutes, prices, 4 VS 1.
Let the picture name the subject so the words can do something else.
Accent one word, the promise (FREE, 5 MIN, DONE).
Keep the title for search words: product, task, platform, version.
Take fonts, colors and the logo from the brand kit in /thumbs/brand.json.
dont: Repeat the title word for word.
Lead with process words (INSTALLING, CONFIGURING, PART 1). A small GUIDE label is fine.
Bullet lists, sentences or more than 6 words.
Version numbers, part numbers, file names or menus: they belong in the video.
Claims the video does not show early (times, prices, counts).
A year as the main idea. A small year tag is fine on evergreen tutorials.
Filler like ultimate, insane, revolutionary, game-changing.

patterns.use: Tutorials where the viewer ends up owning or running the thing.
Only when it really is that short; time it in the video first.
Guides where the whole path costs nothing.
Events, contests and group moments, with the real number from the session.
Two people or two options in one frame, where the picture is the hook.
End-state proof: the finished result with real names and numbers on the card.

recipes.name: Promise + subject anchor
recipes.when: Tutorials and how-to videos. The subject sits on the right of the background, the promise on the left. Use FREE or a time only if true.
recipes.why: The pattern behind the 20x+ server guides in the observed examples: the subject's art or logo as anchor, one outcome phrase, one accent word.

recipes.name: Two together, tagged
recipes.when: Videos about doing something together, or about two options side by side. The background is a footage frame (media id) with both subjects in it; put a tag over each.
recipes.why: P1/P2 tags (6.4x) and name-tagged pets show 'together' without a headline (observed, one niche); multiple people beat one (measured, second hand).

recipes.name: The number is the hook
recipes.when: Events, contests and group moments with a real, impressive count (40 PEOPLE, 4 VS 1). Accent the number.
recipes.why: A huge 4 VS 1 (7.6M views, 4.5x) and a crowd of avatars under a three-word label sell scale in one read (observed, one niche).

recipes.name: The end state
recipes.when: Tutorials and launches: show the finished result the viewer wants, with an info card (a short label, a title, a line of detail). Real names and numbers from the video only.
recipes.why: Outcome over process: a prompt, one arrow and the finished dashboard (32.7x), and a logo-to-result diagram, show the result and not the steps (observed, one niche).

recipes.name: The moment, no words
recipes.when: Moments and funny clips where one frame tells the story. The background must be a footage frame (media id).
recipes.why: Three characters fleeing together need no text (observed); 1of10 reports gaming outliers with no text at all (vendor).

recipes.name: Before to after
recipes.when: Videos about a change. Left image: the before frame. Right image: the after frame. Set both to footage frames (media ids).
recipes.why: Before and after with one arrow: a beginner guide at 4.4x and a prompt-to-dashboard video at 32.7x (observed, one niche).

recipes.name: Centered poster stack
recipes.when: Any vertical cover: Shorts, TikTok, Reels. Adapt the YouTube winner's idea, do not shrink its layout.
recipes.why: Grids crop the top and bottom and add counts; playback UI eats the sides and bottom. A centered stack from 22% down survives all of them.

recipes.name: 4:5 feed card
recipes.when: Instagram and Reddit image posts announcing a launch, an event or a tutorial.
recipes.why: 4:5 gets the most feed height; the square-grid fallback means words stay in the middle 1080x1080.

recipes.name: Wide link card
recipes.when: X and Reddit posts, and link cards for docs or store pages. The small line under the headline says what the thing is, in full.
recipes.why: X shows link cards with no headline, so the image must carry the message; the domain label covers the bottom left.

references.title: YouTube Thumbnail Study: What 500 Breakout Thumbnails Reveal (vidIQ Research)
references.note: Measured. 500 breakout videos, 30 niches, 10K+ sub channels, month to 30 Jun 2026. Faces in 69% (80% of top 50), high contrast 56%, face or high contrast 89%. 72% had overlay text, median 5 words; 28% no text, 52% used 0 to 3 words. Exaggerated expressions only 5%. Descriptive, no control group.

references.title: What makes a good YouTube thumbnail? We analyzed 507,478 videos (Eden)
references.note: Measured. 2,960 thumbnails, breakout (2x+ channel baseline) vs underperformer, Aug 2025 to Aug 2026. Faces 84.2% vs 82.2% (noise). 4 to 6 words 30.6% vs 26.5% (largest gap); 7+ words 29.6% vs 31.1%. Text repeating the title verbatim 6.3% vs 6.8%. Brightness, contrast, saturation, warm share: no difference. Drawn arrows/circles 41.8% vs 38.1%. Observational, no split by niche. Author in page metadata not verified.

references.title: Do Faces Help YouTube Thumbnails? Here's What The Data Says (Search Engine Journal, on 1of10 data)
references.note: Measured (second hand). 1of10 analysis of 300K+ viral 2025 videos using outlier score (views / channel median). Faces and no faces perform similarly overall, vary by niche; multiple faces beat a single face; a face helped only above an unstated channel size.

references.title: YouTube Thumbnail Trends 2026 (1of10 blog)
references.note: Vendor opinion with few numbers. Judges thumbnails at about 120 px wide, says winning palettes use about 3 colors and that gaming outliers often carry no text. No sample sizes: treat as observed, not measured.

references.title: Test titles and thumbnails (YouTube Help)
references.note: Official. Up to 3 titles, thumbnails or combinations. Winner picked on watch time share, not CTR. Results: Winner, Performed same, Inconclusive. Page undated, read Nov 2026.

references.title: Test & compare thumbnails (YouTube Help)
references.note: Official. Up to 3 thumbnails, judged on watch time share. Very similar variants take longer or end without a winner. Desktop Studio, not for Shorts. Page undated, read Nov 2026.

references.title: How to succeed in MrBeast production (Simon Willison's notes on the leaked guide)
references.note: Quotes the guide: CTR 'dictates what we do for videos'; 'I Spent 50 Hours In Ketchup' beats 'In My Front Yard'. Title and thumbnail set the expectation; a mismatch hurts retention. Leaked document, authenticity not officially confirmed.

references.title: MrBeast internal production guide leaked: key points (Tubefilter)
references.note: Coverage of the same guide: CTR, average view duration and average view percentage as the core metrics. Seen in search results; leaked source.

references.title: How a Gaming Channel Grew from 5K to 50K Subscribers in 6 Months (OutlierKit)
references.note: Single vendor case study: thumbnail redesign (game art, reaction face, 2 to 3 words) took CTR from 4.2% to 7.8% in 6 weeks. Unverified, one channel, year not confirmed. Seen in search results.

references.title: The new rules of YouTube from Paddy Galloway (Colin and Samir)
references.note: Packaging first: the idea and its title/thumbnail decide the video. Seen in search results only, no numbers. Year uncertain.

references.title: YouTube thumbnail and title attention, eye tracking (ETRA 2018, Yangandul, Paryani, Le, Jain)
references.note: Academic eye-tracking study coding fixations on thumbnail vs title while people browse for videos: both are read together. Older than 2023, small lab sample.

references.title: YouTube ends 2-year wait for Shorts thumbnails but blocks A/B testing (PPC Land)
references.note: Custom Shorts thumbnails from 25 Jul 2026 (desktop upload). Shown on the homepage and channel Shorts tab, not in the Shorts feed. No A/B testing for Shorts. Says the usable area is 'closer to 3:2' (unclear, unverified).

references.title: About video ad specs: vertical video safe zone (Google Ads Help)
references.note: Official SVG for 1080x1920 Shorts placements: keep clear 288 px top, 672 px bottom, 48 px left, 192 px right. Playback UI, so it matters for the first frame more than for a cover.

references.title: In-Feed Ads specifications and safe zone files (TikTok Ads Help)
references.note: Official 720x1280 safe zone template, scaled to 1080x1920: about 240 top, 660 bottom, 120 each side; action rail inside the right margin from y 840. Playback UI.

references.title: Instagram Reels ads guide (Meta)
references.note: Official: leave 14% top (about 269 px), 35% bottom (672 px) and 6% each side (65 px) free of text and logos. Playback UI.

references.title: Safe zones tool (Socialync)
references.note: Tabulates Shorts 288/672/48/192 and TikTok 240/660/120/120 for 1080x1920; measured the TikTok rail as 180 px wide from y 840 off TikTok's file (their measurement, not TikTok's). Read 11 Oct 2026.

references.title: Instagram's grid change (Buffer)
references.note: Feb 2025: posts preview at 1080x1350 (4:5), Reels at 1080x1440 (3:4) in the grid; some users still see the square grid, so keep key elements in the center 1080x1080.
